en: "It's okay~{w}Professor Warmoni is the bad one, after all~{w}So show us your bad side, right here~"{w}

"...Ha ha, you got me.{w}When did that happen, I wonder?"{w}{p}"It was a pain, but I kept helping the students with their problems... and before I knew it, I was taking the job seriously..."{w}{p}"Figuring I've gotta really think about these kids' futures, y'know?{w}...Right, I've made up my mind!"{w}
note: Editorial: 'Like,' left the clause dangling; 'Figuring' carries the quoted thought (tte, sa) on from the previous sentence.

en: "Just for now, the bad Professor Warmoni is back!{w}Hand over that Mont Blanc!!"{w}
note: Source 'leave it here' rendered as a mugger's 'Hand over'.
Mont Blanc = item ITEM.CSV 673/ITEM_TEXT 665 (chestnut cupcake); same form as slice 051.

en: "Let's see...{w}I feel sorry for you, so here, have this~"{w}
"No, don't use that! Don't you dare use it, got it!?"{w}
"Then I'll teach you the beauty of evil!{w}I'll beat it right into your hides!!"{w}
note: Refusal branch: Warmoni picks a fight. | Editorial: 'into your bodies' unidiomatic; 'beat it into your hides' keeps sono mi ni in Warmoni's thug register.
Star symbol dropped (ASCII only), as slice 032 did.
Subject 'we': both teachers fought the party (Warmoni concedes next row).

en: "Tch... You're not bad.{w}That's the first time in ages I've gotten serious...{w}Well, I'll let you off this time."{w}
Professor Harmoni and Professor Warmoni left.{w}
"Yo, what's up?{w}Dying to walk the bad path, are ya?"{w}

note: Precedes a party-member selection.
Menu choice; the four lessons share the 'Undetectable' frame (source: 'without getting caught').
Hayaben: eating your packed lunch during class, before the lunch break.
Daihen: answering roll call for an absent classmate. 28 chars.
Kebyou: faking illness.

en: "All right, come over here! Time for hands-on training!!"{w}
"Yeah, that's a good mug you've got now!{w}From here on, keep marching down the bad path!{w}Lesson over!!"{w}
"What, you're quitting?{w}Geez, what a gutless little chickenshit."{w}
note: Source idiom (lit. 'small butthole') = petty/gutless; crude, kept crude.
Name box; glossary Mage (class); same as monster name.

en: "You lot, never make light of elemental attack power!"{w}{p}"Raise the fire element of your attacks, and even {11:0001:0001} could burn down an entire country with ease!!"{w}{p}"...Sorry, that was a bit of an exaggeration.{w}But it's a fact: the more you raise elemental attack power, the stronger the effect!!"{w}{p}"And the ones who benefit most from elemental attack power are us mages!"{w}{p}"Long live spells!!"{w}
note: {11:0001:0001} is a spell-name insert (presumably the first, weakest mage spell).
New name box (monster name, MON_TEXT 213).

en: "The spell system we mages use is known as the Reading school of magic."{w}{p}"We interfere directly with a higher space and release its power into the lower space--that is, this land."{w}{p}"The mana consumed in that process is great.{w}Study and theory can reduce it to a degree, but in the end it comes down to the caster's own strength."{w}{p}"Now then, 'higher space' is merely a term of convenience.{w}Just where it really is, no one knows."{w}{p}"Though there's no doubt it is a world where the will of the gods is at work..."{w}{p}"The gods hate it when we mages freely wield even the slightest bit of the power of their world.{w}Hence, as a rule, there are no divine miracles for us."{w}{p}"{11:0001:0017} is the exception, but one cannot call forth that miracle without offering oneself as the price."{w}{p}"...But to wield immense power with your own hands--what could be more alluring than that?"{w}{p}"The other courses could hardly imitate that, I daresay...{w}Afeh...{w}Afehfehfehfehfeh!!"{w}
note: 'Reading school of magic' from katakana riidingu (could also be 'Leading'); source 'katei' read as process. Afeh = toothless old-man laugh kept as sound. | Accuracy: 'jiyuu ni suru' = freely use/control, not 'take liberties with' (disrespect). | Editorial: Awkward 'of us mages' / 'where it refers to' smoothed; 'paying for it with oneself' clarified as offering oneself as the price; invented 'heh' replaced by old-man 'I daresay' (-karou te).
Glossary.
Parentheses kept: whispered aside.
Glossary.
Glossary.

en: "The potency of healing spells depends on your holy-element attack power."{w}{p}"Also, Priests who reach High Master get a spell power boost from it."{w}
note: High Master as in slice 034; spell power boost = JOBABL 'Spell Power UP'.
This student speaks casual-polite (-ssu); rendered with a blunt 'sir'.

en: "I've been wondering for a while, sir... is there any point to holy defense?"{w}

note: Editorial: 'yes?' read oddly; 'right?' carries the unsure yo?

en: "Is there really a point to it?"{w}

note: Editorial: 'because' went beyond the source (sore wa, ja na); now a pure stall.

en: "Truth is, there ain't any point to it, is there, sir?"{w}
note: Editorial: Voice: the -ssu student's rough nee/-ssu kept ('ain't', 'sir') as in 3052/3056.
'for that' makes explicit what the student implies: the spell insert already covers breath defense.

en: "Aaaaah, oh no!{w}I-I just remembered something urgent!!{w}We'll continue the lecture another day--argh, farewell!!"{w}

note: Subject restored as 'the teacher' (Bishop's gender not established).

New name box: goblin temporary lecturer. 17 chars (over ~16); alternative 'Goblin Lecturer' (15) drops 'temporary'. | Editorial: Name box over 16 chars; 'Temp Prof' abbreviates temporary lecturer (Prof as in glossary note 'Prof. Harmoni').

en: "In other words, the spirits stir up the mana of this land just enough to keep it circulating."{w}{p}"It's thanks to the spirits, y'see, that mages can cast spells the same way anywhere they like, anytime."{w}{p}"Priests are under the gods' protection from the start.{w}Since they're loved by beings outside the land, they receive blessings wherever they are."{w}{p}"And then there's alchemy, known as the Ground spell system.{w}That one makes use of the land's mana circulation."{w}{p}"All sorts of research is being done, but for now each alchemist gets results with their own techniques. Someday it'll all have to be merged and weeded out, eh."{w}
note: 'Ground spell system' (katakana guraando), matching 'Reading' in 3044.

en: "That's why I told him to use the lavatory before we came.{w}Well, when I picture him somewhere, desperate and blubbering, searching for him becomes quite a pleasure."{w}
"Hey, even when we find him, we won't call out to him right away, right?{w}Mirco's so funny when he's flustered."{w}
"My, Elpina.{w}You're starting to catch on, aren't you?"{w}
note: Editorial: 'finally' added impatience; dandan = gradually -> 'starting to catch on'.

en: "I've been studying your methods, Sis.{w}Hee hee..."{w}
note: Source writes 'nee-san' with the ordinary kanji here (usually the 'ane-san' variant); both rendered 'Sis'.
As Gurtia's 'Ufufufu' in slice 005.

en: "Is it just me...?{w}I feel like some weird people have snuck into this school..."{w}
"...How come?"{w}{p}"{11:0001:000D} and {11:0001:0014} have the same effect, don't they?"{w}
note: The two inserts are presumably the single- and multi-target versions of one spell (see 3106).

en: "They do not!"{w}{p}"Listen. With spells that come in single-target and multi-target versions, the single-target one has higher power or success rate but only hits one enemy, while the multi-target one has lower power or success rate but can take on several."{w}{p}"If you want to be sure of taking down one enemy, you should attack with the single-target one."{w}
"Still not convinced? Are you stupid or something?"{w}
"...L-love spells... even if you keep aiming at just one person... a-are they still hard to make work?"{w}
"Weren't you listening to me? It's the same with {11:0001:0040}!{w}Even against a strong enemy, if you can charm them, you've got a shot at winning!"{w}
"A-all this time, you...!{w}I've been watching yooouuu!!"{w}
note: Senpai (she is his senior) folded into 'you'; the year gap is clear from 3138. | Editorial: 'it's been you' read as identifying a culprit; fragment now mirrors the source (all this time, senpai...!).

en: "Oh, yeah.{w}Well, of course you have. I've been using {11:0001:003E}."{w}
note: 'you have' answers 3124 (he has been watching her): her spell insert draws his gaze.
Insert moved for English word order.
Bakyuun = gunshot sound (heart-shot gesture); musical note -> '~'.

en: "Heh heh. I'll be waiting, so hurry up and move up a year, okay?"{w}
"It's no use, I just keep choosing remedial classes!{w}Even though I have to move up a yeeear!!"{w}
